bodyFit.source: Dedicated CRJ200 source mesh. Overall length 87 ft 10 in from general drawing. Nose overhang is an illustrative 1.8 m source fit. Tail reference is an illustrative midpoint of the related ER clearance range (6.20-6.32 m), not a standard-weight measured attitude. Attachments are illustrative. Nose attachment reaches the retained gear-bay roof where the source has an open belly cutout. The renderer may raise the target attitude to maintain 150 mm clearance; neither attachment nor height changes wheel centers. Bombardier CSP A-020 Rev 8, January 10 2016; PDF pages 22 (standard CRJ100/200 weight column), 24 (general dimensions), 26 (ER/LR clearance ranges), 97 (standard loaded tire pressures and footprint). https://customer.aero.bombardier.com/webd/BAG/CustSite/BRAD/RACSDocument.nsf/51aae8b2b3bfdf6685256c300045ff31/ec63f8639ff3ab9d85257c1500635bd8/$FILE/ATT1ES4H.pdf/CRJ200APMR8.pdf

units.notes: Manufacturer-selected loading variant; takeoff and ramp/taxi weights are separate. Loads use MTOW with an assumed 95% main-gear allocation. Loaded/in-service values for the standard 47,700 lb taxi-weight column; ER and LR service ranges are not mixed into this entry. The footprint is not to scale: the 158 in outside dimension does not reconcile with 125 in track, 17.4 in pitch and 9 in tire width. The selected manufacturer footprint is explicit; the Aircrafter/FAARFIELD-derived 128.6 in track is a conflicting cross-check. No outer width is asserted. Dedicated FlightGear airframe; uniformly scaled illustrative overlay, not manufacturer CAD. Source proportions and engine details are retained, not used for engineering dimensions.

bodyFit.source: Dedicated CRJ1000 source, with both CF34 engine submodels at the archived XML offsets. Overall length uses 1543.4 in rather than its inconsistent 39.133 m conversion. Tail reference 7.649 m and nose overhang 1.73 m from general drawing. Rigid source fit and attachments remain illustrative. Nose attachment reaches the retained gear-bay roof where the source has an open belly cutout. The renderer may raise the target attitude to maintain 150 mm clearance; neither attachment nor height changes wheel centers. Bombardier CSP D-020 Rev 8, December 17 2015; PDF pages 25 (weights), 31 (dimensions), 108 (footprint and unloaded tire pressures). https://customer.aero.bombardier.com/webd/BAG/CustSite/BRAD/RACSDocument.nsf/51aae8b2b3bfdf6685256c300045ff31/ec63f8639ff3ab9d85257c1500635bd8/$FILE/ATT82VLY.pdf/CRJ1000APMR8.pdf

units.notes: Manufacturer-selected loading variant; takeoff and ramp/taxi weights are separate. Loads use MTOW with an assumed 95% main-gear allocation. Manufacturer UNLOADED inflation values, not loaded service pressures. Uniform contact pressure equated to inflation is a modeling approximation. The footprint retains FS228.40/FS819.38 from a shorter variant; their difference does not reproduce its dimensioned 742 in wheelbase. The 160.40 in footprint track differs slightly from the 160 in general drawing and 160.18 in workbook. Imperial footprint labels govern. Dedicated FlightGear airframe; uniformly scaled illustrative overlay, not manufacturer CAD. Source proportions and engine details are retained, not used for engineering dimensions.
